# http-schema

> A parser for HTTP schema DSL. Declarative RESTful API configuration -> flat callable functions.

## Documentation

- [Main README](README.md): Project overview, installation, and usage guide
- [DSL Requirements](docs/01-requirements.md): DSL syntax rules and examples
- [Architecture Analysis](docs/02-old-xx-principle.md): Previous version architecture overview

- [Parser Design](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-http-schema-parser-design.md): Full parser architecture and design

- [Typed API](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-http-schema-typed-api.md): Multi-type typed API routing with resolveType

## Features

- [Basic Usage](docs/features/01-basic-usage.md): DSL definition & create API instance
- [RESTful Resources](docs/features/02-restful-resources.md): Auto-generate CRUD endpoints from `resources`
- [Typed API](docs/features/03-typed-api.md): Multi-business-line isomorphic endpoints via `type` + `resolveType`
- [Path Params](docs/features/04-path-params.md): Path placeholders `{id}` / `:param`
- [Prefix & Suffix](docs/features/05-prefix-suffix.md): Function name prefix/suffix with group override
- [Interceptors](docs/features/06-interceptors.md): Request interceptors & `transformResponse`
- [Schema Config](docs/features/07-schema-config.md): Full `httpSchema` options reference
- [DSL Rules](docs/features/08-dsl-rules.md): Complete DSL rule reference

## Usage

Declaratively define an HTTP API schema, then call it as flat typed functions.

```ts
// 1. Define the schema (schema.ts)
export default {
  baseURL: '/api',
  request: ['', 'json'],
  items: [
    { resources: ['badges'] },                       // auto CRUD
    {
      request: ['/v1', 'json'],                       // group path prefix
      items: { profile: ['get', '/me'] }              // leaf: [method, path, config?]
    }
  ]
};

// 2. Create the API instance (api.ts)
import httpSchema from '@jswork/http-schema';
import { FetchAdapter } from '@jswork/universal-request-adapter-fetch';
import schema from './schema';

const api = httpSchema(schema, {
  adapter: new FetchAdapter(),
  transformResponse: (res) => res.data,
});

// 3. Call endpoints
await api.badges_index();            // GET    /api/badges
await api.badges_show({ id: 1 });    // GET    /api/badges/1
await api.badges_create({ title: 'x' }); // POST /api/badges
await api.profile();                 // GET    /api/v1/me
```

### Key concepts

- **`items`** is dual-state: an *array* groups child nodes (nested `request`/`items`/`resources`); an *object* maps leaf function names to `[method, path, config?]` tuples.
- **`request: [prefix, format]`** — group-level path prefix, inherited downward; `format` maps to `dataType`.
- **`resources`** — string array auto-generates 5 RESTful endpoints (`{name}_index/_show/_create/_update/_destroy`); object array supports `only`/`except`.
- **Path placeholders** — `{id}` and `:param` are replaced from request data; remaining fields become the body (or query string for GET/HEAD/DELETE).
- **`prefix` / `suffix`** — append to generated function names, inherited with override.
- **Typed API** — group with `type` keeps original leaf keys; call `api.typed(key)(data)` and `resolveType(data?, options?)` dynamically routes to the current business type.
- **Interceptors** — `interceptors: [{ request, response }]` hooks plus a global `transformResponse`.
